newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Eurobourses slump, dlr soars after Greenspan.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Eurobourses slump, dlr soars after Greenspan.

text.p: European and American bourses slumped on Thursday after U.S. central bank chief Alan Greenspan was seen to give his clearest warning yet that U.S. rates might be increased for the first time in two years.
But it was good news for the dollar, which soared less than two hours after slipping on data showing a ballooning U.S. trade gap.

Federal Reserve Chairman Greenspan said that low inflation was needed for a healthy economy and warned: "If we allow that (infltaion) to get away, we will...have set in motion a set of forces that which bring the...recovery to an end".
Analysts saw his comments as signalling the U.S. central bank was inching towards tightening credit, possibly as soon as next week.
"It is clear the economy is growing strongly and that is the environment in which you would expect a pre-emptive rate hike," said Tony Norfield, treasury economist at ABN AMRO.
The dollar immediately jumped on Greenspan's remarks. by late trading in Europe it was up a pfennig from its European close on Wednesday, above 1.69 marks, and it approached the 124 yen level.
In prepared testimony to Congress's Joint Economic Committee, Greenspan said the economy retained a "great deal of vigour" and the jobs market was strong.
And, as he has done before, he stressed the importance of the Fed acting promptly -- or ideally, preemptively -- to keep inflation low.
The central bank's policy-making Federal Open Market Committee meets on Tuesday to consider raising short-term rates.

Earlier the dollar hit the day's lows after U.S. data showed the trade gap soared for a second consecutive month in January, hitting its highest level in more than nine years on record imports and shrinking exports.
The January deficit was much higher than anticipated by Wall Street economists.
"I think it's clearly a surprising figure," Adam Chester, an international bond analyst at Yamaichi International (London), said.
"(The figures) highlight the fact that the improvement that we saw in the trade balance in the U.S. in the fourth quarter has come to a startling halt."
The effect of Greenspan's remarks came as a blow to European bourses, which had already been well down in morning trading suffering from rate worries and a 19-point fall in the Dow overnight.

By the time most European bourses closed the Dow was off its lows but still down around three quarters of a percent, London closed down around 1.75 percent, Germany closed electronic trading 1.5 percent off (floor trade had already closed down 1.5 percent) and the Paris bourse had also tumbled well over 1.5 percent before business ended.

Britain's blue chip FTSE 100 index suffered its biggest one-day fall in point terms of the year so far. It closed 74.1 points lower at 4,258.1, its biggest loss since an 88-point tumble last December.
Andy Hartwill, stock market strategist at brokerage SocGen, said the FTSE 100 could drop as low as 4,150 in the short term -- some seven percent below its record 4,466.3 set on March 11.

"The possibility of an interest rate hike is exposing high stock market valuations in the UK and the United States," Hartwill said. "But I would be happy to buy the market not far below its current level."

Dealers said concerns about rates had been depressing the market and keeping buyers at bay all day and lower-than-expected British retail price inflation figures and a batch of encouraging corporate results failed to lift the gloomy tone.

In Germany the main market focus was the restarting of trade in Thyssen and Krupp-Hoesch after two days of suspension related to Krupp's attempt to produce a merger of their steel businesses. By the close of trade shares in both companies had moved strongly ahead.
CURRENCIES AT 1630 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.6910 marks and 123.73 yen, compared with Wednesday's late European levels of 1.6808 and 122.59.
STOCK MARKETS CLOSING INDICES
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index closed down 74.1 points at 4,258.1.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed down 51.26 at 3,264.67.
PARIS - The CAC-40 closed down 43.05 points at 2,553.72.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed at $351.60 versus London's close of $348.95 on Wednesday. Silver ended three cents lower at $5.18.
